acceptance_criteria: A fresh, never-sealed store: `sl read <v>` continues to render with NO seal banner by default (byte-identical to pre-slice output) unless the arbiter decision (open question) opts the built-in fold lens into showing one; regardless, `render_context["cut"]` for that read reports `{"available": True, "anchor": None, "sealed_to_head": False, "tick_total": 0}`.
A store whose head fact IS the latest tick's `fact_cursor` (fully sealed, e.g. Sol's 694/694 case): `cut["available"] is True`, `cut["anchor"]` is the last tick, `cut["sealed_to_head"] is True`.
A store with a sealed tick followed by newer unsealed facts: `cut["available"] is True`, `cut["anchor"]` names the last tick, `cut["sealed_to_head"] is False`.
An aggregate (combine/discover) vertex: `sl read <agg>` does not raise; `cut == {"available": False, "reason": "aggregate vertex — no single witness cut across members", ...}`.
A vertex with no store / store not yet created: read still succeeds; `cut["available"] is False` with a stated reason, never a crash and never a guessed 'live unsealed' claim.
`sl read <v> --json` (no --at/--as-of) carries a top-level `cut` key with the same shape as above, for both the Surface gate-pass path and the gate-fail (custom-lens/--lens-override) path.

`sl read <v> --at head` continues to behave exactly as today (existing `cursor` key/behavior/tests untouched) AND additionally carries `cut` derived from the same already-resolved witness position (no extra store I/O).
`sl read <v> --as-of ...` continues to behave exactly as today; `cut` reports `available: False` with a reason naming event-time projection as the cause (no witness-anchored cut in that mode).

A lens (built-in or custom) that declares a `cut` kwarg in its `fold_view` signature receives the populated dict via `call_lens`'s existing signature-filtered kwarg dispatch (`apps/loops/src/loops/lens_resolver.py:481-510`) with zero changes to that dispatch mechanism.

A new shared helper (`cut_line` or equivalent) exists in `apps/loops/src/loops/lenses/_grammar.py` that renders all three states honestly (sealed cut / live head with history / genuinely unavailable) and is exercised by a unit test asserting it never emits any 'live unsealed'-shaped claim when `available is False`.

All existing golden snapshot tests under `apps/loops/tests/golden/` remain green with zero `--update-goldens` diffs (proves the substrate change is additive/inert for the default render path, per whatever the arbiter decides in the open question below).
current_behavior:
Sol's homelab-audit consumer lens (external, `gruel.network/.loops/audit/lenses/homelab_audit.py:385-464`, NOT part of this repo) demonstrates the exact failure the friction names: `build_doc(state, projection: ProjectionMeta | None = None)` defaults `projection=None`, and when None, line 396 renders `f"Live unsealed fold: {fact_count} current nodes."` unconditionally — a positive false claim from missing data. Its own `fold_view` (line 452-464) never passes a `projection` because nothing in loops's read path ever hands one to it.

Inside strange-loops itself: `apps/loops/src/loops/cli/dispatch.py:226-390` (`dispatch()`) resolves a lens and calls `call_lens(lens_fn, render_data, zoom, width, **extra)` where `extra = dict(op.render_context)` (line 337) plus `vertex_name`/`vertex_path`/`visible`/`chars`/`lines`. For the `read`/`fold` verb, `op.render_context` is built in `apps/loops/src/loops/cli/views/fold.py:733-736` as `{"piped": ..., **({"cursor": cursor_meta} if cursor_meta is not None else {})}`, and `cursor_meta` is ONLY computed (line 608-616) `if args.at or args.as_of`. On an ordinary `sl read <vertex>` (no --at/--as-of — the dominant path), `render_context` carries no seal/tick provenance key at all — not `cursor`, not anything else. `apps/loops/src/loops/surface.py`'s `Surface`/`Row`/`Window` dataclasses (lines 62-138) likewise carry zero seal/tick fields. So today, no consumer lens (built-in or custom) can obtain honest seal-cut data for a plain read without reaching around loops and querying the store directly (exactly what Sol's `publish_homelab_audit.py` does, and what the same review flagged as friction #2: "no public sealed-projection/export API exists").

The built-in `fold_view` (`apps/loops/src/loops/lenses/fold.py:379-421,187-223`) is itself NOT buggy today: it only renders a provenance banner (`cursor_mode_line`/`_cursor_lines`) when `cursor is not None`, which happens only for explicit `--at`/`--as-of` reads, and its "no anchor" case (line 217, `"unsealed tail — no prior tick anchor"`) is honest because it only fires on an ALREADY-resolved witness position. The bug is entirely a substrate-absence problem: nothing analogous exists for the default live-head read, so any consumer who wants that disclosure (as two independent N=2 consumers now have) has no honest data source and reaches for a guess.

The engine already holds everything needed to answer this honestly at read time, reused from the existing --at machinery: `engine.witness.resolve_witness_position(store_path, "head")` (`libs/engine/src/engine/witness.py:275-360`, already invoked for `--at head` via `apps/loops/src/loops/cli/witness_address.py:178-179`) returns a frozen `WitnessPosition` whose `.anchor` (`TickAnchor | None`, witness.py:146-161) is "the last sealed tick at-or-before this position, or None" — `None` here is a genuine, confidently-known "never sealed" fact, not an unavailability signal. `WitnessPosition.fact_id` compared to `anchor.fact_cursor` tells you, at zero extra query cost, whether the live head IS exactly the sealed cut (fully sealed) or sits beyond it (live tail). `engine.store_reader.StoreReader.tick_total()` (`libs/engine/src/engine/store_reader.py:64`) gives a cheap total-tick count. None of this is wired to the default read path today."
dependencies: None on other 0.9.0 slices — this is self-contained within apps/loops's CLI read path and reuses existing, already-shipped 0.8.0 engine primitives (resolve_witness_position, TickAnchor, StoreReader.tick_total). Does not touch libs/atoms, libs/lang, or libs/custody.

This module already owns exactly this kind of vertex_path→WitnessPosition translation for --at (`is_aggregate_vertex` line 43, `resolve_at_address` line 151), so this is additive, not a new module.

In `run()`, alongside the existing cursor_meta block (lines 605-616), add an independent `cut_meta = _resolve_cut(...)` call (new local helper, or call `witness_address.resolve_cut` directly) that: reuses `at_position.anchor`/`at_position.fact_id` when `--at` is active (no extra I/O); marks `cut` as `available: False` with an event-time reason when `--as-of` is active; otherwise resolves fresh via the new `resolve_cut(vertex_path)`. Thread the result into the `render_context` dict built at lines 733-736 under a new `"cut"` key, unconditionally (not gated the way `cursor` is).

Mirror the existing `cursor_meta` JSON-merge pattern for the new `cut` key in both JSON branches: the gate-pass branch (`to_dict(surface)` payload, lines 312-322) and the gate-fail branch (`_render_foldstate_json`'s `extra` dict, lines 182-213, 325-328). No change needed to the plain-text dispatch machinery itself (`extra: dict(op.render_context)` at line 337 already forwards `cut` to `call_lens` for free via the existing signature-filtered kwarg mechanism).

Add the shared render-honesty helper (e.g. `cut_line(cut: dict, width: int | None) -> Block`) implementing the three-state contract: available+sealed_to_head → "sealed…"; available+anchor+not sealed_to_head → "live head — N sealed tick(s) behind it…"; available+anchor is None → "live head — unsealed tail, no prior tick anchor" (reuses the exact phrase already proven honest in `lenses/fold.py:217`); available is False → "seal status unavailable…" (+ reason). This is the module `_grammar.py`'s own CLAUDE.md designates for exactly this: "Never hand-roll… a timestamp format, a width=None guard, or a header card in a lens — import it from here" — same discipline applies to this new honesty-ladder primitive so no future lens (built-in or, on next contact, Sol's) re-derives its own None-defaulting logic.

open_questions: Should the BUILT-IN fold lens (`apps/loops/src/loops/lenses/fold.py::fold_view`, the output of plain `sl read <vertex>` with no flags) start VISIBLY rendering the new cut/seal disclosure by default, or should the substrate ship data-only (available to any lens via render_context/JSON, but silent-by-default for the built-in TTY/piped render, exactly as it is today)? This is a genuine fork, not an implementation detail, because: (1) `dispatch.py`'s existing wiring for the sibling `cursor` kwarg unconditionally prepends `cursor_mode_line` above the fold body whenever the kwarg is non-None (fold.py:414-421) — if `cut` followed the identical pattern and were wired to always render, EVERY `sl read` invocation across the whole CLI would grow a new banner line, which is a highly visible UX change and would require re-baselining the entire golden-snapshot suite (`apps/loops/CLAUDE.md`: "Golden snapshot tests lock output across all 4 zoom levels"); (2) leaving it silent-by-default (my recommendation, given `decision:design/drop-truncation-from-human-reads`-style precedent of not eagerly cluttering default reads, and given `horizon`/`orient` already own dedicated venues for seal-state disclosure) means the fix's practical benefit is scoped to consumers who write or declare a lens that opts in — real for Sol/siftd-shaped consumers (the two N=2 evidence sources), but a plain `sl read project` user gets no visible change. Needs Kyle's call on which failure mode is worse: silent-by-default under-delivers on 'ordinary terminal reads' per the friction's own wording, versus always-on risks feeling noisy/changes output everywhere. A middle option (gate the banner to -vv/FULL zoom only, or only when NOT `sealed_to_head`) is available but is itself a further sub-choice worth deciding alongside this one, not something to default silently.

planned_changes.description: Add `resolve_cut(vertex_path: Path) -> dict` to `apps/loops/src/loops/cli/witness_address.py`. Reuses `is_aggregate_vertex` (line 43) to short-circuit aggregates with `{"available": False, "reason": "aggregate vertex — no single witness cut across members"}`; otherwise resolves the store path (reuse `loops.commands.resolve._resolve_vertex_store_path`, already imported this way in `cli/views/fold.py:302`) and, when a store exists, calls `engine.witness.resolve_witness_position(store_path, "head")` inside a broad try/except (any `WitnessResolutionError` subclass, or any other Exception) that degrades to `available: False` with a reason string rather than propagating — an informational-provenance failure must never break the read itself. On success builds `{"available": True, "anchor": {"name", "ts", "fact_cursor"} | None, "sealed_to_head": bool, "tick_total": int}` where `sealed_to_head = anchor is not None and anchor.fact_cursor == position.fact_id` (zero extra query — both values are already on the resolved `WitnessPosition`) and `tick_total` comes from `engine.store_reader.StoreReader(store_path).tick_total()` (a cheap COUNT, store_reader.py:64).

In `apps/loops/src/loops/cli/views/fold.py::run()`, after the existing --at/--as-of cursor_meta block (lines 605-616), compute `cut_meta` unconditionally: reuse `at_position.anchor`/`at_position.fact_id` (zero extra I/O) when `at_position is not None`; set `{"available": False, "reason": "event-time projection has no witness-anchored cut"}` when `as_of_ts is not None`; otherwise call the new `resolve_cut(vertex_path)`. Add `"cut": cut_meta` to the `render_context` dict at lines 733-736, unconditionally (not gated on `is not None` the way `cursor` is — `cut` should always be present once computed, since 'unavailable' is itself a meaningful, honest value distinct from 'key absent').

In `apps/loops/src/loops/cli/dispatch.py`, extract `cut_meta = op.render_context.get("cut")` alongside the existing `cursor_meta = op.render_context.get("cursor")` (line 310), and merge it into both JSON branches exactly as `cursor` is merged today: the gate-pass `to_dict(surface)` payload (lines 312-322) and the gate-fail `_render_foldstate_json` call's `extra` dict (lines 325-328).

Add `cut_line(cut: dict, width: int | None) -> Block` to `apps/loops/src/loops/lenses/_grammar.py`, implementing exactly the three/four states enumerated in `current_behavior` and `acceptance_criteria` (sealed-to-head / live-with-history / never-sealed / unavailable), reusing the existing honest "unsealed tail — no prior tick anchor" phrase from `lenses/fold.py:217` for the never-sealed case so wording stays consistent across the two related banners. This is the ONE place that owns the never-guess-from-None discipline for cut/seal data — any lens (built-in, at whatever zoom the open question resolves to, or an external consumer like a rewritten Sol lens) should call this instead of hand-rolling its own default.

risks: Broad try/except around `resolve_witness_position` in the new `resolve_cut` could accidentally swallow a genuine bug (e.g. a real engine regression) and misreport it as 'seal status unavailable' rather than surfacing it. Mitigation: catch the specific `WitnessResolutionError` family plus a narrowly-scoped fallback, and consider logging/counting the fallback path in tests so an unexpected-exception case is caught in CI rather than silently degrading forever.

If step 5 (built-in fold_view rendering) is taken without care, it changes output for every `sl read` across the whole test suite and any downstream consumer (hooks, session-orient scripts, other agents' tooling) that scrapes plain-text output — `apps/loops/CLAUDE.md`'s own history flags this exact failure mode (the orient hook's shell-grep breakage documented in `commands/orient.py`'s module docstring). Any golden-updating pass must be reviewed line-by-line, not bulk-approved.

`sealed_to_head` conflates 'this exact fact is the tick's fact_cursor' with `store verify`'s broader 'N facts covered by the union of all tick windows' metric (`commands/store.py:295-299`) — these usually coincide for a store that seals sequentially via a `when=seal` boundary but are NOT proven identical in every topology (e.g. a boundary that doesn't fire on every fact, or multiple interleaved boundary series). The banner text must say 'sealed at tick X' (a true, narrow claim) rather than implying store-wide seal coverage parity with `store verify`'s number — misphrasing here would reintroduce a milder version of the same honesty bug this slice fixes.

The new `cut` JSON key is additive and none of the existing JSON tests do full-dict equality (confirmed: `test_fold_view_cursor.py` asserts via `payload["cursor"][...]` key lookups, and no JSON goldens exist under `apps/loops/tests/golden/goldens/`), but any future JSON consumer doing strict schema validation elsewhere (outside this repo, e.g. Sol's publisher) would see a new key appear — purely additive, non-breaking by construction, but worth a one-line mention wherever the JSON contract is documented if such a doc exists.

thesis: Ordinary `sl read` (and any consumer-authored lens) currently receives ZERO seal/tick provenance for the default live-head read — the render_context channel that carries this kind of disclosure (\"cursor\") exists and is honest, but is wired ONLY for explicit --at/--as-of reads. Two independent consumers (homelab-audit 2026-07-12, siftd 2026-07-18) hit this absence and, lacking any real data, guessed wrong (\"Live unsealed fold\" rendered from a None default, contradicting `store verify`'s 694/694 sealed). This slice threads the SAME witness-position machinery already used for `--at head` into every default read (as a new, additive `cut` render_context/JSON key, decoupled from the --at/--as-of refusal-gating machinery so it can never regress custom-lens compatibility), and ships one shared, honest three-state rendering helper so no lens — built-in or external — has to hand-roll (and get wrong) its own None-defaulting logic again.</thesis>
